Time scales and history features available in a hazard formula

Source: R/intervals.R
time_scales.Rd

The right-hand side of a transition formula is evaluated on the interval-expanded data. Besides the columns of data, the following variables are available.

Time scales

tstart, tend

Boundaries of the current interval on the process time scale. The hazard is constant on (tstart, tend].

t

Alias of tend: time since the origin of the process ("clock forward"). The hazard of an interval is evaluated at its end, the same convention under which piecewise exponential models are fitted, so a hazard specified here and one estimated from the simulated data refer to the same time point.

t_entry

Time at which the current state was entered.

t_sojourn

Time spent in the current state, tend - t_entry ("clock reset").

interval

Index of the current interval in cut, so that a hazard given as one value per interval can be used directly: ~ log(rates[interval]) + 0.3 * x.

History features

n_transitions

Number of transitions made before the current one.

n_visits_<state>

Number of visits to <state> so far, including the current state.

t_total_<state>

Time spent in <state> before the current interval.

A process whose hazards use only t is Markov; one that uses t_sojourn is semi-Markov; one that uses the history features is neither.
